text:
leah: quick report — intermittent client-side JSON.parse errors in our JS sampleapp while streaming. repro when network blips / auth refresh happens. stack: browser fetch-based stream, sdk@0.9.3, staging behind haproxy + ELB.

leah: symptoms: after reconnect the stream parser occasionally receives a buffer that starts with a stray \"\r\n{\" which ends up getting stitched onto the previous partial 'data:' payload and fails JSON.parse.

jen: do we have any raw capture? hex dump or curl -N would help. this sounds like a framing/line-break normalization problem.

leah: pasted a small curl run from staging (masked):

```
$ curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer x" "https://staging.redwood.io/stream/.."
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
:
: keepalive
data: {"id":"1"}\n\n\r\n{"id":"2"}\n\n
```

leah: note the explicit CRLF between the separated chunks. our parser expects \n\n as separator and treats the bare leading `{` as continuation.

tom: FYI haproxy has a tendency to coalesce small TCP writes; same with ELB NLB -> target. Also when we abort+reopen connections (auth refresh path) partial buffers can be left in JS runtime state if we don't clear them.

diego: what's the client parse logic now? naive split by "\n\n"?

leah: yep. simple stateful buffer: append new bytes, find "\n\n", split, for each event split lines and parse data: lines that start with 'data:' are concatenated and JSON.parse on the joined payload. no CRLF normalization.

jen: short-term fix: normalize CRLF to LF globally on incoming bytes before doing splits. ignore leading lines starting with ':' (keepalive), and when a fetch is canceled because of auth refresh, discard any partial event buffer.

tom: long-term: support last-event-id on reconnects and do a strict boundary reset on abort. also consider switching to EventSource polyfill in browsers where fetch streaming is flaky.

leah: PR incoming — added normalize(/\r\n/g, "\n"), ignore ':' lines, and explicit discardPartialOnAbort flag. Unit tests simulate: quick abort + reconnect, interleaved keepalives, and CRLF-inserted chunks. coverage added for parse loop.

leah: local perf: error rate from 6% -> 0.6% on a 10k-iteration flapper test. still seeing extremely rare case when auth refresh is ~30ms and proxy coalesces writes in odd way.

diego: can you capture tcpdump at the edge to confirm which component is inserting CRLFs? also check TLS terminator (if using ALB) -- sometimes it normalizes line endings on health-checks or other rewrites.

leah: planning to spin up a repro with haproxy configured both with and without http-keep-alive buffering. i'll try proxy_buffering-like toggles on nginx and equivalent on haproxy: 'option http-keep-alive' toggles and tune 'tune.bufsize'.

tom: also audit our SDK abort flow: when token refresh triggers, are we calling controller.abort() and then immediately reconnecting? if so, the same microtask loop may merge buffers across the re-request. We should schedule reconnect on next tick and clear buffer synchronously.

jen: agree. small change: clear state immediately on abort, then setTimeout(() => reconnect(), 0) to ensure next request gets fresh V8 buffers. Add a comment in code.

leah: CI ran the branch fix/stream-boundary-normalize — all tests passed on Node 18 + bundle build. ci-bot: build passed (14/14) :white_check_mark:.

diego: once PR lands, backport to 0.9.x patch and add note in sampleapp README about flaky networks. also add a short troubleshooting snippet: how to curl -v -N and what to look for (">> \r\n leading chunks").

tom: we should also instrument SDK to emit a metric when parse errors occur (counter) and tag with 'reconnect=true' if it happens within X ms of an auth refresh. that helps gauge customer impact.

leah: adding metric in PR. will flag it as P2 because it can crash unguarded consumer code. creating GH issue and linking PR.

jen: nice. follow-up: consider server-side convention: always emit an explicit blank data line (\ndata:\n\n) as a hard separator after every event to make parsers more robust. But that's heavier weight.

diego: open question — do we want to special-case leading '\\r' before '{' when concatenating and attempt to repair? i.e., trim leading non-printables before JSON.parse. could help but feels hacky.

leah: i prefer normalizing line-endings + discard-on-abort first. dodgy repair heuristics risk hiding real bugs.

jen: agreed. keep fix conservative, add defensive checks and metric so we can detect future regressions.

leah: gist with repro + test harness: https://gist.github.com/redwood/stream-boundary-repro (private). assigning follow-ups: @tom check edge proxy config, @diego add metric + backport task, @jen merge PR + changelog blurb.

ci-bot: PR fix/stream-boundary-normalize merged to main. release pipeline triggered. :rocket:

leah: thanks everyone — will monitor metric after deploy and open follow-up if we still see >0.1% parse errors.
